title: Metro Central Municipal Waste & Recycling Authority Guidelines

preparationSteps: Remove plastic lid and place lid in Recycling / Blue Bin
Do not place coated cup body in paper recycling; dispose in Landfill
rules.sourceExcerpt: Single-use hot beverage cups with poly-coat linings are not accepted in blue bins; place in black bin (Landfill / Residual Waste).
Rigid plastic drink lids labeled #1 through #5 are recyclable in the Blue Bin once separated from disposable cups.

preparationSteps: Screw cap back on to prevent litter
rules.sourceExcerpt: All #1 PET clear and colored plastic beverage bottles are accepted in the Blue Bin. Caps may remain attached.
Aluminum beverage cans are 100% recyclable in the Blue Bin. Please rinse out remaining sugary sodas or juices.
Clean, dry corrugated cardboard and shipping boxes are accepted in the Blue Bin. Flatten boxes to conserve truck capacity.

preparationSteps: Place directly in Green Organics Bin or paper bag
rules.sourceExcerpt: All fruit and vegetable food waste, including banana peels and rind, must be segregated into the Green Bin for municipal composting.

preparationSteps: Place greasy cardboard in Green Bin
rules.sourceExcerpt: Pizza boxes with grease, cheese, or food residue cannot be recycled in blue bins; place them in the Green Bin for composting.

preparationSteps: NEVER place in blue curbside bin
rules.sourceExcerpt: Plastic film bags wrap around sorting machinery at the MRF. Do not place in curbside bins; take them to designated retail depot drop-off points.

preparationSteps: Tape exposed battery terminals with clear tape to prevent short circuits
Bring to Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) depot or red battery kiosk
Never put in regular bins due to fire hazard
rules.sourceExcerpt: Household and rechargeable batteries pose serious fire hazards in garbage trucks and are strictly prohibited in curbside bins. Deliver to HHW depots or red battery kiosks.
Expanded polystyrene foam (Styrofoam) food containers and packaging are not processed locally and must go into the Landfill bin.

preparationSteps: Lids may be recycled separately in Blue Bin
rules.sourceExcerpt: Clear, green, and brown container glass jars and bottles are fully accepted in the Blue Bin after a light rinse.
Chip bags and candy wrappers composed of plastic laminated with metallic foil cannot be separated and belong in the Landfill bin.

preparationSteps: Wrap broken ceramic pieces securely in thick newspaper or cardboard to protect handlers
Do NOT place in the blue container glass bin (ceramics contaminate glass recycling melt)
Place in designated municipal inert rubble drop-off or general residual waste
rules.sourceExcerpt: Broken ceramic coffee mugs, porcelain dishes, and stoneware have a different melting point than container bottle glass and must be wrapped and disposed in inert mineral waste.

preparationSteps: Ensure all remaining pills or tablets are removed
Take expired or unused pills to a pharmacy take-back drop box
Dispose of the empty aluminum/plastic blister packaging in residual sanitary waste
rules.sourceExcerpt: Pharmaceutical blister packaging composed of heat-sealed aluminum foil and PVC plastic cannot be separated by curbside facilities and belongs in dedicated pharmaceutical or sanitary disposal.

preparationSteps: Ensure garments are clean and dry
If wearable, donate to charity collection bins or clothing drop-off boxes
If torn or stained, place in textile recycling drop-off kiosk for fiber recovery
rules.sourceExcerpt: Clean clothing, cotton t-shirts, and household textiles should never be discarded into general waste; deposit in authorized municipal textile recovery bins.

preparationSteps: Back up and wipe personal data if disposing of phones or computing devices
Do NOT place electronics or cables in blue recycling or curbside trash
Drop off at certified e-waste recycling kiosks or electronics retail take-back programs
rules.sourceExcerpt: All consumer electronics, smart devices, cables, and circuitry must be diverted to authorized E-Waste drop-off collection stations for precious metal recovery and toxic component diversion.
